title: POC scoping - workload modeling (Cedarbank)
summary: Kickoff POC scoping focused on workload characterization and traffic modeling for a Cedarbank LLM-based customer support feature. Discussed QPS targets, concurrency, distribution of input/output token lengths, benchmark plan (latency/cost/quality), security constraints (VPC, KMS, audit logs), success criteria, and a tentative 6-week pilot timeline. Agreed next steps: Redwood to share sample benchmark harness, security docs, and a proposed cost/runbook; Cedarbank to provide telemetry from prod traffic and anonymized prompt samples.
topics: Benchmark plan and metrics (p95 latency, cost per 1k tokens)
Deployment mode (hosted vs dedicated vs private)
next_steps: Redwood: share benchmark harness + sample scripts by 2027-08-02
Cedarbank: export 2 weeks of anonymized traffic and top 500 prompts by 2027-07-30
Schedule latency benchmark (dry-run) with Cedarbank infra on 2027-08-05
Agree final success criteria and SLOs in follow-up by 2027-08-06
action_items: Samir Patel - send benchmark harness link and cost estimate - due 2027-08-02
Carlos Ruiz - export anonymized traffic (2 weeks) + token histogram - due 2027-07-30
Lena Ortiz - prepare initial model recommendations and quantization profile - due 2027-08-04
Aisha Malik - confirm KMS/HSM requirements and compliance contacts - due 2027-08-03
transcript: 00:00 - Samir Patel: OK folks good afternoon, thanks for joining. I'm Samir from Redwood, AE on this account, and with me is Lena from our SE team. How's everyone doing?
00:06 - Maria Chen: Hi Samir, doing well. Thanks. Carlos, Aisha and I are on. Super keen to scope the POC - we want to make sure benchmarks reflect real traffic, not just synthetic tests.

00:18 - Lena Ortiz: Totally, that's our goal. Today we want to capture QPS, concurrency, token distributions, and success criteria. We'll propose a benchmark plan that maps to cost/latency/quality tradeoffs.

00:30 - Carlos Ruiz: Quick context - Cedarbank runs the chat support stack on k8s in GCP, around 120k monthly conversations. Peak concurrent sessions roughly 1,200, but user messages are short on average. We currently send data to a hosted LLM API for prototyping but we need lower p95 latency and better cost predictability for production.
00:52 - Samir Patel: Great. Can you share current QPS numbers and average tokens in a sample? That will help us recommend batching and whether Dedicated or Private makes sense.

01:05 - Carlos Ruiz: We have an average QPS of about 20 across business hours, spikes up to 80 for short bursts, p99 spikes up to ~140 QPS during incidents. Average input tokens ~18, output tokens ~45, distribution is skewed - many short, some long threads.
01:26 - Maria Chen: And latency target is p95 under 350ms ideally, p99 under 700ms. Cost target is below $0.70 per 1k tokens equivalent for this phase, otherwise exec will push back.
01:39 - Lena Ortiz: Understood. A couple of clarifying questions: are you planning streaming responses for UI, and do you require conversational KV cache across turns?

01:47 - Maria Chen: We want streaming in the UI for perceived latency. KV cache across a session would be nice but for POC we can scope session length to 6 turns max. Also we have strict data residency - EU-only data for some customers, so VPC/private might be required later.

02:02 - Samir Patel: Noted. For the POC we recommend a two-pronged approach: 1) run a hosted benchmark with Redwood's hosted API to measure baseline latency and quality with your prompts, 2) run a Dedicated instance simulating your concurrency and burst profile to estimate cost and per-GPU throughput. If EU residency is needed we can spin a private deployment later.
02:22 - Carlos Ruiz: Sounds good. How do you model bursts? We need the bench to reflect p99 bursts and queueing effects.

02:29 - Lena Ortiz: We take your real traffic trace - anonymize then replay it with preserved inter-arrival times and token lengths. We run several scenarios: 'steady', 'peak', and 'incident spike' where QPS increases 3x for 10 minutes. That shows queuing, batching, and p95/p99 behavior.

02:45 - Maria Chen: OK then. On models: we evaluated a couple open models, and are curious if Redwood recommends smaller quantized models for cost reasons or a heavier model for quality. We can't have hallucinations for account info queries.

02:58 - Lena Ortiz: Right. For fact-grounded agent tasks we usually recommend a model with a larger context and higher base quality; for short push-button answers a 7B quantized with dynamic batching might be cost-optimal. We'll include a recommendation matrix showing expected latency and token cost per 1k tokens for each candidate model.
03:13 - Carlos Ruiz: Can you give an example throughput number? Like QPS per GPU for a 7B quantized model at 512 context?

03:20 - Lena Ortiz: Rough rule of thumb: a single A10/A100-like GPU with optimized runtime can do around 60-120 QPS for short-inference scenarios with continuous batching for a 7B quantized model at small prompt sizes - but that's very workload-dependent. We'll provide benchmark numbers using your token distribution.
03:38 - Maria Chen: And for longer contexts or multi-turn we should expect lower QPS due to KV cache growth, yes?

03:44 - Lena Ortiz: Exactly. As context window grows the per-token compute increases and KV cache memory becomes a factor; batching efficiency also changes because longer requests take longer to finish and reduce batching headroom.

05:02 - Samir Patel: ... so the success criteria we usually propose are: p95 latency target met in the selected deployment mode, cost per 1k tokens under your threshold, and quality measured by a small eval set where Redwood matches or beats baseline - Maria is that ok?
05:15 - Maria Chen: Yes, quality must be within 5% of current baseline on our eval prompts. Also need audit logs and SSO integration for compliance.
05:24 - Aisha Malik: On the security front: SOC2 is required, we need to validate that logs and KMS integration meet our internal policy. Can Redwood support customer-managed keys and HSM?

05:33 - Samir Patel: Yes - Customer-managed KMS/HSM is supported on Private and Dedicated flows; hosted has envelope encryption and Redwood-managed KMS by default but we can discuss HSM options for Private.
05:44 - Aisha Malik: Good. Also need RBAC and per-route logging for the audit trail.
05:49 - Lena Ortiz: That's supported - we'll attach our security deck and SOC2 report. We'll also provide example audit log schemas.

06:02 - Carlos Ruiz: Back to traffic model: our traffic is diurnal with a weekday peak at 14:00 UTC, average QPS 20, baseline concurrency about 300 sessions but we care about peak concurrency ~1200. Token histogram: 60% under 25 input tokens, 30% 25-60, 10% >60 with outputs similar but output tails heavier. We can share a CSV.

06:26 - Samir Patel: Perfect. That histogram is exactly what we need to estimate batching efficiency. For example, if 60% of requests are very short, we can use aggressive micro-batching to improve throughput without hurting p95.
06:38 - Maria Chen: What about cold start for dedicated pods when burst arrives? We can't have 10s of seconds of cold start.

06:45 - Lena Ortiz: We configure warm pools and fast scaling policies for Dedicated; for hosted we have multi-tenant warm capacity and automated fallbacks. We'll propose autoscaling policy options that meet your p95 SLO and limit cost impact.
07:00 - Maria Chen: Also would like to see cost sensitivity: e.g., if we accept p95 500ms vs 350ms what cost delta do we expect?

07:07 - Samir Patel: We'll include a sensitivity table: latency SLO vs required vCPU/GPU counts and estimated monthly token cost. We'll also show quantization tradeoffs and caching effects (prefix and KV).

07:18 - Carlos Ruiz: For the POC duration and milestones we prefer a 6-week pilot: week 1 data handoff and harness setup, week 2 dry-run hosted benchmarks, weeks 3-4 Dedicated runs and tuning, week 5 quality eval and security review, week 6 decision and handoff. Is that realistic?
07:32 - Lena Ortiz: That timeline aligns with similar pilots. The critical path is getting the anonymized traffic and model prompts. If we get those by Friday we'll hit week 2 dry-run on schedule.
07:40 - Maria Chen: We can get the export by Friday. A note - some prompts include PII, so we'll need to redact at source or provide a minimized sample.
07:50 - Samir Patel: Understood. Provide our data-handling guide; we can accept prepared CSVs or you can run our anonymization script in your environment and share output.
08:00 - Aisha Malik: We'll likely run the anonymization in-house and share the result. Also I'll need to run your security team through our compliance questionnaire - can we get a point of contact?
08:08 - Samir Patel: Yes, I'll share Lena's contact and our security pack. Lena, you'll be the SEC/SE POC?
08:14 - Lena Ortiz: Yep I'll handle the technical and security touchpoints.
08:20 - Carlos Ruiz: One more on benchmarks: we want p95 latency measured end-to-end including network overhead to our region. How do you instrument that?

08:27 - Lena Ortiz: We can run the load generator from your VPC to the Redwood endpoint and measure client-side latencies; for Dedicated/Private we can run inside your infra. We'll produce a breakdown: client network, queuing, model compute, and post-processing.
08:40 - Maria Chen: And quality evaluation - we have a 250-sample eval set with human labels. We'll want automated eval metrics plus a manual spot check.
08:48 - Samir Patel: Sounds good. We'll run our eval harness against same prompts and provide per-prompt diff and a small rubric for human review.
09:05 - Carlos Ruiz: On pricing - for Dedicated you provide committed tiers. Can you provide an estimate based on our token volumes?

09:12 - Samir Patel: We'll send an initial cost estimate; for POC we usually offer a limited trial credit and then a short-term reserved capacity recommendation if needed. We'll include per-1k-token pricing across model families and a Dedicated hourly estimate.

09:25 - Maria Chen: Ok. For the acceptance criteria to move to an internal pilot we'll need: 1) p95 < 350ms on hosted dry-run or equivalent on Dedicated, 2) cost below $0.70 per 1k tokens (or clear path to get there), 3) quality within 5% of our baseline on the eval set, 4) security sign-off on KMS/logs.
09:45 - Samir Patel: We'll write that up as proposed success criteria and send it for sign-off. If any of those change we can iterate.
10:00 - Aisha Malik: Timing-wise we need security sign-off by week 5, otherwise procurement windows slip into next quarter.
10:08 - Lena Ortiz: We'll prioritize the security packet.
10:15 - Maria Chen: Last question: do you support canary routing or fallback to smaller models during overload?

10:21 - Samir Patel: Yes - Redwood supports policy-based routing and automatic fallback to compatible model variants or lower-cost tiers when capacity constrained. We'll show a routing policy example.
10:34 - Carlos Ruiz: Great. Recap of commitments?

10:37 - Samir Patel: Redwood to share: benchmark harness + runbook, security deck and SOC2, initial model recommendations and cost sensitivity table by Aug 2. Cedarbank to share anonymized traffic and eval set by July 30. Schedule dry-run benchmark for Aug 5.
10:55 - Maria Chen: That's correct. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email.
11:02 - Samir Patel: Thanks all, talk soon.
11:06 - [call ends]
